text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: high error rate detected on /v1/embeddings (prod, us-east-1) — 5xx spike at 12:11 UTC. Routing to on-call.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout 'canary-2026-03-09' started at 12:09 UTC for model redwood-mini-v2-quant (variant q4_0). Currently running on 3% of traffic.

anna: I’m on it. acknowledging pager. looking at traces and metrics now.

mike: saw the spike too. errors look like NaN outputs converting to 5xx in the embeddings service stack. stack traces point to runtime kernel applying quantization path.

sarah: tagging @emma for infra-level resource contention? Not sure if GPUs OOM or bad math.

emma: checked node metrics — memory and GPU util look normal. cluster logs show repeated "invalid_float" warnings coming from the model runtime around 12:10.

anna: ok this seems model-specific. does traffic pattern match canary?

mike: yes — errors correlate exactly with requests routed to canary-2026-03-09. non-canary traffic steady.

jake: recommend immediate kill-switch on canary routing. we have a feature-flag to flip. can someone run the flag?

anna: on it. running flag command.

anna: ```
# flip the canary off
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  https://console.redwood-inference.internal/api/flags/traffic-routing \
  -d '{"canary_id":"canary-2026-03-09","state":"off"}'
```

ops-bot: Feature flag update accepted. Canary routing set to OFF for canary-2026-03-09. Effective immediately. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Canary traffic removed. Rolling traffic back to baseline model variant (redwood-mini-v2-fp16).

incident-bot: Notifying customers with impacted requests count. Estimated affected requests: ~12k over 4m window. Users: internal-analytics, search-service, embeddings-batch.

sarah: pushing rollback and scaling stable variant to absorb traffic. monitoring 5xx and latency.

mike: quick debug note — reproduced locally with the q4_0 quantized binary when sequence length > 1024, NaNs appear during attention kernel. filing a follow-up.

emma: infra changes: warmed 6 extra instances of stable variant to 200% capacity for 15min to soak traffic.

anna: status update for pager: now 5xx rate returning to baseline. error count dropping. estimate mitigation at 12:16 UTC.

mike: can we push emergency rollback in control-plane to make sure no residual canary assignments exist in edge caches?

deploy-bot: Running global rollout-revert job:
```
run_job --id=rr-2026-03-09-canary-revert --targets=edge-proxies --wait
```

deploy-bot: Job completed at 12:18 UTC. Edge proxies reconciled.

jake: thumbs up. any customer-facing action required? SL seat for internal-analytics alerted support earlier.

sarah: I’ll create a quick incident note for accounts and support with affected windows and approximate QPS and request ids.

anna: handing off to next on-call @mike for postmortem and follow-up. I need to jump to a customer call. mike — please coordinate with model-team (sarah) and runtime (jake/emma).

mike: taking handoff. timeline so far: 12:09 canary rollout -> 12:11 spike detected -> 12:13 kill-switch -> 12:18 edge reconcile complete -> 12:20 5xx baseline. Will own blameless postmortem and RCA.

sarah: initial mitigation actions: feature-flag flip, rollback to fp16 variant, warm-up of instances. Root cause suspected: quantization path in q4_0 produces invalid floats for long sequences.

jake: next steps: create a canary gating test for sequence-length edge cases + add a quick synthetic regression test that runs q4_0 with seq=2048 on a CI GPU before rollout.

emma: infra follow-up: add automated canary traffic shadowing to catch runtime warnings (invalid_float) and escalate before 5xx.

mike: customer impact note draft: "Between 12:11-12:18 UTC, ~12k requests across embeddings endpoints routed to a canary variant experienced 5xx errors. No PII exposed. We reverted the canary at 12:13 and completed edge reconciliation at 12:18. Customers may see transient failures during that window."

anna: thanks — please post that to #incidents and ping the affected account managers. I’ll update the on-call log. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Created incident ticket INC-2026-428 in the tracker and linked this thread.

mike: logging action items: [1] model-team to produce failing unit test for q4_0 (sarah), [2] runtime to add NaN detection + fail canary early (jake), [3] infra to add traffic shadowing (emma), [4] ops to add automatic rollback threshold on errors > 2% for 1m (anna/ops). Assigning owners.

anna: leaving note — if anything spikes back up ping oncall escalation, otherwise mike will own follow-ups.

incident-bot: Incident resolved (mitigated) at 12:20 UTC. Severity: Sev-2.

mike: thanks team. I’ll kick off the postmortem doc and schedule a quick sync with model/runtime tomorrow.

sarah: adding a few logs and stack traces to the ticket now.

emma: monitoring for 30m; will escalate if anything anomalous.

jake: adding CI gate within the hour.

anna: back to normal ops. great coordination. :sparkles:
